statement: Figure 1 A selection of our contributions focusing on subclasses of perfect graphs. In addition, the paper establishes the NP-hardness of planar graphs with bounded degree and degeneracy, and provides an exact formula for the length of sequences (and hence linear-time algorithms) in paths and cycles. The complexity of SymISR for bipartite graphs and distance-hereditary graphs remains open; we leave this as a future direction.

Given a polytope 𝑃 ⊆ R𝑛 described by 𝑂 (𝑛) inequalities with 0/1 coefficients and two vertices 𝑢, 𝑣 of 𝑃, the length of a shortest path from 𝑢 to 𝑣 in the skeleton of 𝑃 cannot be approximated within a factor of (1 − 𝜀) ln 𝑛 in polynomial time for any fixed constant 𝜀 > 0, unless P = NP. Moreover, the same reduction can be equipped with a suitable linear objective function to show that the relevant paths are monotone.
